materials.effect: Part snaps under bending or impact load along layer lines
materials.cause: Anisotropic FDM layer bonding weak along Z-axis print direction
materials.action: Reorient print angle by 45-90 deg or increase wall perimeter loops

materials.effect: Corrosion thin-out and localized stress concentration
materials.cause: Uncoated carbon steel exposed to ambient humidity/moisture
materials.action: Specify protective plating (zinc), powder coat, or switch to 304/316SS

materials.effect: Loss of joint clamping force, hinge loosening, or dimensional drift
materials.cause: Continuous compressive loads over time, severely accelerated by operating temperatures above 60°C (140°F)
materials.action: Implement metal compression limiters (sleeves) in bolted joints or utilize Belleville spring washers to maintain tension

materials.effect: Fastener permanently seizes during installation or maintenance, requiring destructive removal
materials.cause: Friction-induced localized heat destroying the passive oxide layer during threaded engagement
materials.action: Apply anti-seize compound (molybdenum disulfide), use rolled threads instead of cut, or mix alloy grades (e.g., 304 nut on 316 bolt)

materials.effect: Optical crazing (fogging) and rapid brittle fracture propagation
materials.cause: Chemical attack from anaerobic threadlockers (Loctite), alcohol, or high installation torque
materials.action: Ban chemical threadlockers near part; specify thread-forming screws designed for plastics (PT screws)

materials.effect: Loss of dimensional tolerance and up to 30% reduction in tensile strength
materials.cause: Absorption of atmospheric moisture over time
materials.action: Design with looser tolerances or switch to moisture-resistant POM (Delrin)

materials.effect: Cracking, loss of elasticity, and sealing failure
materials.cause: UV/Ozone exposure or thermal cycling driving out plasticizers
materials.action: Verify specific elastomer compatibility with operating environment (e.g., EPDM for UV)

components.effect: Loss of joint clamp load and physical attachment failure
components.cause: Over-torquing in raw plastic/3D printed holes without brass inserts
components.action: Incorporate brass heat-set inserts (M3/M4) into 3D printed bosses

components.effect: Splitting or radial bursting of the mating component
components.cause: Wedge geometry of the screw head driving extreme outward radial forces into the material (highly lethal to plastics/composites)
components.action: Switch to pan head, socket head, or button head screws with flat washers to distribute load parallel to the axis

components.effect: Vibrational self-loosening and subsequent joint failure
components.cause: Re-use of the nut causing permanent plastic deformation and wear of the nylon collar
components.action: Add explicit assembly note: 'Do not reuse Nyloc nuts after initial installation', or specify deformed-thread all-metal locknuts

components.effect: Loss of sealing pressure resulting in fluid or pressure leak
components.cause: Thermal degradation of elastomer or gap clearance too large for operating pressure
components.action: Verify gland fill percentage (typically 70-85%) and specify backup rings if >1500psi

components.effect: Increased friction, acoustic noise, vibration, and kinematic seizure
components.cause: Lubrication starvation, particle contamination, or exceeding dynamic load rating
components.action: Specify sealed bearings (RS/ZZ) or schedule lubrication PMs

components.failure_mode: Tooth Root Bending Fatigue / Abrasive Wear
components.effect: Backlash increase, skipped teeth, or catastrophic transmission loss
components.cause: Cyclic overload, misalignment, or inadequate surface hardness
components.action: Specify case hardening (carburizing/nitriding) for gear teeth

components.effect: Loss of return force preventing mechanism reset
components.cause: Operating stresses exceeding torsional yield or cyclic fatigue limit
components.action: Shot peen springs for high-cycle applications; ensure design stays below 45% tensile strength

components.effect: Increased Equivalent Series Resistance (ESR), voltage ripple, and thermal runaway circuit failure
components.cause: Sustained operation at elevated ambient temperatures (component lifespan halves for every 10°C increase per the Arrhenius equation)
components.action: Derate operating temperature spec by 20°C, ensure PCB airflow, or switch to solid polymer/tantalum capacitors

components.effect: Exponential increase in contact resistance resulting in localized housing melt/fire
components.cause: Mechanical micro-vibrations wearing away the tin/gold plating, exposing the base copper alloy to oxidation
components.action: Apply dielectric grease, specify higher micron plating thickness, and secure wiring harnesses with strain relief within 50mm of the connector
